G003_guava = Google Guava core libraries (~610 java files in guava/src). Java 21 + Maven 3.9 present but **build needs network** (offline `./mvnw` fails: central-publishing-maven-plugin + all deps uncached in ~/.m2). So no full build/test — verify refactors by reading + standalone `javac` against hand-written stubs for external annotations (com.google.common.annotations.GwtCompatible, base.Function/Preconditions, errorprone.annotations.*, org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable).

**Two flavors maintained in lock-step**: `guava/src/com/google/common/...` (JRE) and `android/guava/src/com/google/common/...` (Android). For escape package the files were byte-identical across flavors — apply same edit to both (cp jre→android). Also `guava-gwt/src-super/.../super/` holds GWT super-source twins, but ONLY for classes needing GWT-different emulation (e.g. escape/Platform.java has a GWT twin with non-ThreadLocal buffer). Don't put generic logic in Platform — it forces a needless GWT-twin edit.

NOTE: most apparent duplication in Guava is INTENTIONAL — don't "fix" it. primitives/*Array expandedCapacity + */checkNoOverflow are pasted per-class on purpose (source comment "Unfortunately this is pasted from ImmutableCollection.Builder.") to avoid cross-package deps; Ascii.toUpper/toLowerCase + PercentEscaper UTF-8 branches + ArrayBased escaper fast-paths are deliberately inlined/unrolled for perf. Good targets = genuine missed dedups with a NATURAL home (shared superclass) or local cleanups that don't fight a design decision.

REJECTED candidate (don't re-investigate): hash/`shiftMix(long val){return val ^ (val>>>47);}` is byte-identical in FarmHashFingerprint64 + Fingerprint2011 (both extend AbstractNonStreamingHashFunction, only 2 subclasses). DO NOT pull up — these are independent faithful C++ ports of Geoff Pike's algorithms (their K0/K1/K2 constants DIFFER), each inlines `x^=x>>>47` in some spots and uses shiftMix in others (local algorithm detail, not shared util), and AbstractNonStreamingHashFunction is a purpose-neutral structural base (Hasher plumbing, no algorithm constants) — injecting magic constant 47 there is wrong. Textbook intentional-independence. An Explore sweep for identical-helper-across-siblings-with-shared-superclass found this as the ONLY candidate in escape/math/base/hash/io/primitives/net/html/xml — i.e. the verifiable-package dedup well is essentially dry after refactors #1-#3. A SECOND sweep (dead private members + redundant-recompute-within-method, same packages) found NOTHING — code is exceptionally clean (e.g. Strings.commonSuffix repeated .length() is fine: O(1)+JIT-inlined). Also confirmed math/Stats+StatsAccumulator ALREADY consolidate their shared helper (calculateNewMeanNonFinite is one pkg-private static in StatsAccumulator, imported by Stats) — upstream had done that pair; #3 fixed the one they missed (PairedStats). Conclusion for future sessions: do NOT manufacture marginal/design-fighting edits here just to "keep going"; the high-confidence verifiable-refactor space is exhausted.

**Refactor #3 (math pkg): consolidate duplicated ensurePositive/ensureInUnitRange.** PairedStats + PairedStatsAccumulator each had private static `ensurePositive` (identical) and `ensureInUnitRange` (PairedStats hand-rolled clamp; Accumulator used Doubles.constrainToRange — verified bit-exact equivalent incl NaN/±Inf/±0/subnormals). NOT intentional-independence dup (Accumulator already depends on PairedStats via snapshot(); PairedStats has no back-dep). Moved both helpers into PairedStats as package-private static, consolidated ensureInUnitRange on `Doubles.constrainToRange(value,-1,1)` (added Doubles import to PairedStats); Accumulator now calls `PairedStats.ensurePositive/ensureInUnitRange` and dropped its now-unused Doubles import. Home=PairedStats avoids a cycle (Accumulator→PairedStats already exists; reverse would cycle). Both @GwtIncompatible, no super-source twin. Net -46/+14 across 4 files (2 jre+2 android). Verified: standalone bit-exact test (22 edge cases) + 2-class same-package package-private static call reproduction. (Full math stub-compile is heavy — many deps — so verified the touched logic+mechanics standalone instead.)

**Refactor #2 (escape pkg): ArrayBasedEscaperMap.createReplacementArray keySet()+get() → entrySet().** Removed redundant per-entry map.get() hash lookup; added `import java.util.Map.Entry;`. Matches sibling idiom (CharEscaperBuilder.toArray already uses entrySet). Behavior-identical (writes are key-indexed, order-independent). Applied to both flavors. Verified: full escape pkg stub-compiles clean + functional test (Escapers.builder→ArrayBasedCharEscaper, direct ArrayBasedUnicodeEscaper w/ escapeUnsafe, empty map, large keys, shared multi-entry map) all pass. content.text:
Done. Second refactor applied to the `escape` package.

## What changed

`ArrayBasedEscaperMap.createReplacementArray` iterated the map's `keySet()` and then called `map.get(c)` for each key — a redundant hash lookup on every entry. I switched the loop to iterate `entrySet()` directly, reading the value off the `Entry`:

```java
for (Entry<Character, String> entry : map.entrySet()) {
  replacements[entry.getKey()] = entry.getValue().toCharArray();
}
```

This is behavior-identical (writes are key-indexed, so iteration order is irrelevant), eliminates the per-entry lookup, and matches the existing idiom in the sibling `CharEscaperBuilder.toArray`. Added `import java.util.Map.Entry;`. The `max(map.keySet())` call above is unchanged since it genuinely needs the key set.

Applied to both the JRE and Android flavors (byte-identical, kept in lock-step).

## Verification

- **Stub-compile** both flavors → `EXIT=0`.
- **Functional test** driving `createReplacementArray` through `ArrayBasedCharEscaper` (multi-entry HTML-style map, a shared `ArrayBasedEscaperMap` reused across two escapers, empty-map fast path, single-key `max+1` sizing) → **ALL PASS**.

Combined with the earlier `growBuffer` pull-up, the `escape` package now has both high-confidence dedup/cleanup refactors applied. Both are narrow, verified, and behavior-preserving — consistent with the principle that most remaining "duplication" in Guava is intentional and shouldn't be touched.
